title: Quiz: 18.06 Lecture 21: Eigenvalues

questions.question: Which term matches this definition: A nonzero vector x such that A x equals lambda x; the matrix only stretches its direction, it does not rotate it.
questions.explanation: eigenvector: A nonzero vector x such that A x equals lambda x; the matrix only stretches its direction, it does not rotate it.

questions.question: Which term matches this definition: The number ____ in A x = ____ x, the factor by which the matrix stretches an eigenvector.
questions.explanation: eigenvalue: The number lambda in A x = lambda x, the factor by which the matrix stretches an eigenvector.

questions.question: Which condition on A - lambda I gives the eigenvalues of A?
options: Its diagonal entries are all zero
questions.explanation: A nonzero x with (A - lambda I) x = 0 exists only when A - lambda I is singular, i.e. has determinant zero.

questions.question: Which term matches this definition: A matrix is ____ exactly when its determinant is zero.
questions.explanation: singular: A matrix is singular exactly when its determinant is zero.

questions.question: Which term matches this definition: The determinant of A minus lambda I; its roots are the eigenvalues.
questions.explanation: characteristic polynomial: The determinant of A minus lambda I; its roots are the eigenvalues.

questions.question: Which term matches this definition: Matrices like [[2, 1], [1, 2]] whose eigenvectors are always perpendicular.
questions.explanation: symmetric matrices: Matrices like [[2, 1], [1, 2]] whose eigenvectors are always perpendicular.

questions.question: The matrix [[2, 1], [1, 2]] has eigenvalues 1 and 3. What is the product of its eigenvalues equal to?
questions.explanation: The determinant equals the product of the eigenvalues: 4 - 1 = 1 x 3 = 3.

questions.question: Which term matches this definition: The sum of the diagonal entries; it equals the sum of the eigenvalues.
questions.explanation: trace: The sum of the diagonal entries; it equals the sum of the eigenvalues.
